learningObjectives: Identify major cellular and signalling components of neuroimmunity.
Explain adaptive and maladaptive immune effects on neural function.
Recognise red flags for medical escalation.

anatomy.label: Microglia
anatomy.short: Survey and respond within CNS tissue
anatomy.detail: Microglia clear debris and regulate synapses.
anatomy.clinical: Persistent activation may alter plasticity and network function.

anatomy.label: Astrocytes
anatomy.detail: Astrocytes regulate barrier, transmitter and cytokine environments.
anatomy.clinical: Reactive states can be protective or disruptive.

anatomy.label: Blood–brain barrier
anatomy.detail: Endothelium and perivascular cells regulate trafficking.
anatomy.clinical: Barrier dysfunction can amplify central exposure to peripheral signals.

anatomy.label: Cytokines
anatomy.detail: Cytokines alter neural excitability, metabolism and behaviour.
anatomy.clinical: Excess or prolonged signalling can contribute to sickness behaviour.

anatomy.label: Peripheral–central routes
anatomy.short: Link body immune state to brain
anatomy.detail: Vagal, humoral and cellular routes communicate systemic conditions.
anatomy.clinical: Medical illness can alter cognition and mood without primary psychiatric causation.

interaction.title: Explore Neuroimmunology
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence.

stages.label: Detect
stages.text: Pattern-recognition systems identify threat or injury.

stages.label: Signal
stages.text: Cytokines and chemokines coordinate local and systemic responses.

stages.label: Contain
stages.text: Barrier and immune mechanisms limit spread and clear debris.

stages.label: Resolve
stages.text: Active resolution returns tissue toward homeostasis.

quizBank.question: Microglia are best described as:
options: Resident immune-surveillance cells of the CNS
quizBank.explanation: Microglia are CNS-resident immune cells with surveillance, pruning and repair roles.

quizBank.question: Neuroinflammation is:
options: A mechanism that can be adaptive or maladaptive
quizBank.explanation: Its meaning depends on timing, context, intensity and cause.

quizBank.question: Cytokines can influence:
quizBank.explanation: Immune signalling can alter neural and behavioural states.

quizBank.question: An acute psychiatric presentation with seizures and autonomic instability should raise concern for:
options: Possible autoimmune encephalitis or other medical cause
quizBank.explanation: Neurological and autonomic red flags warrant urgent medical assessment.

quizBank.question: The most accurate clinical stance is:
options: Integrate immune mechanisms with broader differential diagnosis
Use cytokines as direct psychological labels
quizBank.explanation: Neuroimmune findings are important but nonspecific.

reviewPrompts: Neuroinflammation is a mechanism, not a diagnosis—and “activated” immune cells are not automatically harmful.
